Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We're lining up a 6-week pilot (internal AI assistant) and need a concrete provisioning proforma and surge strategy for a private VPC deployment. High-level asks:

- Throughput targets: sustain ~1.2M tokens/day with daily peak windows (2x baseline) and expected burst events up to 6x for 3-5 minute windows.
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 180ms for text-gen workloads; model is a 30B decoder-only (avg seq 512).
- Concurrency: typical 120 concurrent active sessions, with spikes to 720 during marketing pushes.
- Availability: 99.95% monthly target for inference API.
- Networking: we need egress constraints documented (our infra team will check), and any cross-AZ traffic assumptions spelled out.

Could you share a one-page proforma with recommended GPU counts/types, autoscale policy, expected token-per-second throughput per GPU, estimated warm-pool sizing, and an outline of network egress/peering implications? Also flag any blocker (eg. 3rd-party kernel limits, quantization caveats).

We'd like that before our architecture review on Thu (Oct 1). If helpful, I can share our traffic projections.

Alex — thanks for the clear asks. Attaching a starter proforma and a short network egress matrix for your infra team. High-level summary below, and I've looped Karthik and Naomi for technical sizing + networking readout.

Summary (TL;DR)
- Recommended baseline: 6 x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs (sustained pool) yielding ~6–7k tokens/sec aggregate for your 30B model under FP16 + kernel optimizations.
- Warm-pool headroom: provision an additional 2 GPUs as hot stand-by to absorb 2x short bursts without cold-start latency (~90s model load).
- Burst coverage: for 6x instantaneous spikes, recommended short-term autoscale to +10 GPUs (total 16) with queueing and graceful degradation rules to preserve p95 SLOs.
- Autoscale policy: aggressive scale-up on queue depth + prefix cache hit-rate; conservative scale-down with a 3–5 minute cooldown to avoid thrash.
- Network: cross-AZ traffic may add 4–8ms tail latency; recommend colocating GPU pool and ingress NAT in same AZ and using a single egress VPC endpoint with bandwidth reservation.

Known caveats: quantized 4-bit variants reduce memory pressure (fits more replicas) but may increase p95 latency variability; warm-up strategies and KV cache priming are essential.

Attachments: 20260930-df-provisioning-proforma.xlsx (spreadsheet), network-egress-matrix.pdf (PDF)

Next steps: Can Karthik and Naomi validate the numbers below and call out any infra/network blockers? Alex — if you can share the traffic projections, we'll iterate and produce a final proforma by Wed EOD. Otherwise we can take this into the Thu architecture review.

Adding technical notes / redlines for the proforma:

- Throughput assumptions: 30B decoder-only at seq=512, batch size 8, kernel-optimized runtime -> ~100–120 seq tokens/s per GPU under FP16; we used 110 for headroom math. If you prefer quantized int8/4-bit runtimes expect 1.6–2.0x throughput but plan for 10–20% p95 variance.
- Warm pool & cache: recommend a 2-stage warm pool: (1) hot replicas (2 GPUs) with KV cache primed for top 500 prompts; (2) warm replicas (4 GPUs) with no KV warm cache — faster to spin up for mid-tier bursts. Include a fast cache-priming job to run during off-peak.
- Autoscale: trigger scale-up when queue depth > 200 or average latency > 80ms for 30s window. Use predictive scaling during planned marketing pushes (pre-warm + job to stage cache).
- Queueing & graceful degradation: implement token-priority lanes (interactive vs batch) and soft-queue rejections with client-backoff guidance. For extreme bursts, fallback to a smaller quantized model with strict rate-limits to keep p95 under 300ms.
- Networking: ensure 25 Gbps NICs per host and allocate minimum 80% of egress bandwidth for inference traffic to avoid head-of-line blocking from logging/metrics streams. Cross-AZ replication of KV caches is expensive; avoid unless low-latency peering is available.
- GPU type: A100-80GB or H100-equivalent recommended for baseline. If budget-constrained, 48GB batches are possible but will increase the required replica count.

Notes on observability + SLOs: instrument per-request token counts, model variant used, cache-hit rate, and quantization flag. Set alerts on sustained queue growth > 5 minutes.

cc: Naomi for network egress numbers.
